title: Moses
summary: In Jewish and biblical tradition, Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt, brought down the law from Mount Sinai, and died at 120 on Mount Nebo after viewing the Promised Land. He is known from religious tradition; the dates c. 1391–1271 BCE come from a rabbinic chronology, not from independent evidence.

uncertainty.note: Dates are those of the Seder Olam Rabbah chronology as cited by the Jewish Virtual Library, a traditional calculation; the figure is not independently dated, so the range is nominal.

where.modern_name: Mount Nebo, Madaba Governorate, Jordan (the mountain where tradition places his death; the exact peak, Ras al-Siyagha or Ras al-Nibaa, is debated)
where.historical_name: Mount Nebo (biblical Nebo/Pisgah), Moab, east of the Jordan River

importance.justification: Central figure of the Torah in the tradition described by the sources.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap Nominatim result for Mount Nebo

reviewer_note: Moses is known only from religious tradition. The Jewish Virtual Library article does not address historicity and I opened no source that does; its footnote ties the dates to Seder Olam Rabbah. Encyclopedia.com says Ras Siyagha is the more likely Pisgah though Ras al-Nibaa kept the name; the pin is the mountain, not one peak.
